subject: Private Offer: list-price residual allocations and channel margin clarification
messages:
From: Procurement (Acme Health) <procurement@acmehealth.com>

Date: 2026-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: private offer structure + channel margin guidance

Hi Sean / Tom,

We're moving forward with the pilot and need clarity on how the private offer will present on our AWS invoice and what the residuals look like for listed vs negotiated list price. Specifically:

- If Redwood lists a discounted private offer through AWS, how are reseller/reseller-passback and reseller margin visible on the invoice?
- We have a distributor in the mix; we need to confirm the cadence of pass-through credits for overage months.
- Can you share a worked example: list price, private-offer net, reseller gross, reseller net?

Attached a spreadsheet with our expected usage profile. Can we get a single-sheet worked example back by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Clara Mitchell
Head of Procurement
Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

Date: 2026-04-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private offer structure + channel margin guidance

Thanks Clara — looping in Ben and Irene who own our marketplace packaging and channel ops. High level answers below; we'll follow up with a worked example and an annotated draft of the private offer PDF.

Quick answers:
- Visibility: AWS shows the marketplace "list price" and the private-offer adjustment line. Reseller commissions are not exposed as a separate AWS invoice line by default — they are settled off-invoice between the partner and the reseller unless you elect a pass-through SKU that routes credit.
- Residuals: The private-offer net (what Acme is billed) is distinct from the marketplace list price. Reseller gross/net depends on whether the reseller is paid from the list price or from Redwood's payable to the partner. The most straightforward is to model reseller remuneration off the private-offer net and then route a collaborator credit.
- Overage cadence: month-of usage true-up is typical; we support monthly true-ups and can trigger a passback credit the next billing month if requested.

Action items:
1) Ben: prepare the worked example (list price -> negotiated net -> reseller gross/net) and a CSV workback.
2) Irene: confirm legal/ops on pass-through SKUs vs off-invoice settlement and whether we can do a monthly passback on this account.
3) Sean: I'll collate and send to Clara with a redlined private-offer PDF.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0118

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, procurement@acmehealth.com, tom.lee@amazon.com

Date: 2026-04-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: private offer structure + channel margin guidance

Hi all — attached is a simple worked example and a pricing_breakdown.xlsx with three scenarios (flat list anchoring, hybrid pass-through, and off-invoice reseller credit). Highlights:

- Scenario A (List anchoring): Acme billed list price less private-offer discount; reseller margin calculated off list price yields a larger absolute reseller payout. This increases partner cost but preserves reseller visibility on marketplace statements.
- Scenario B (Pass-through SKU): We push a dedicated pass-through SKU so reseller credits are visible on the AWS invoice. That requires marketplace packaging and a short approval lead-time.
- Scenario C (Off-invoice): We pay reseller via our partner payments system; Acme sees only the private-offer net. Simplest operationally but less transparent to the reseller.

I've included a worked example row using Acme's attached usage profile (monthly token estimate, peak months). See column G-H for reseller gross/net and column K for timing of passback.

Attachment: pricing_breakdown.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
- Irene confirms which operational path is least friction (pass-through SKU vs off-invoice).
- If Acme needs invoice visibility, we prioritize pass-through SKU and I'll open a PM with AWS (Tom) for packaging SLA.

Ben Carter
Head of Deal Ops | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: irene.choi@redwood.com

Thanks Ben — reviewed the workbook. Operational notes:

- Pass-through SKU: feasible, but requires vendor packaging and an onboarding ticket with AWS marketplace ops. Expect 7-10 business days for SKU approval plus mapping; we can accelerate with a contact at AWS.
- Tax and refunding: passback credits still need reconciliation for tax treatment; we'll need Acme to complete a quick tax questionnaire.
- Evidence: for monthly true-ups we'll emit a monthly passback CSV (sample attached: channel_margin_workback.csv).

Clara — if you want reseller visibility on the invoice, opt for Scenario B (pass-through). If you prefer simplicity and quicker time-to-market, Scenario C is the fastest (we handle reseller payments off-invoice).

Irene Choi
Marketplace & Partner Ops | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
